name: Oaks Park Campground (Ashley NF)
note: USFS campground on the south shore of Oaks Park Reservoir, Ashley NF, ~20 mi N of Vernal then ~14 mi on gravel FR-018. 11 sites (mostly small back-in, a few pull-throughs for larger trailers), picnic tables and fire rings; vault toilets, hand-pump well on the west shore. First-come, first-served (listed on rec.gov but not online-bookable). OHV recreation nearby. --Claude

name: Smith and Morehouse Campground
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Kamas RD, near Oakley/Smith and Morehouse Reservoir (~7,800 ft). 34 paved sites, no hookups; vault toilets, host firewood. Mix of reservable and first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: East Park Campground (Ashley National Forest)
note: Ashley NF, Vernal RD, on the shore of East Park Reservoir (~30 mi NW of Vernal via US-191 + FR 018/020, maintained forest road). 21 sites, vault toilets, no potable water; first-come, first-served (not on recreation.gov). Open June-Sept. --Claude

name: Sulphur Campground
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Evanston RD, Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (UT-150), ~39 mi S of Evanston at ~9,100 ft. 21 sites (15 single, 5 double, 1 group), no hookups, vault toilets. Mix of reservable and first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Lodgepole At Flaming Gorge
note: Ashley NF, Flaming Gorge NRA, on US-191 ~26 mi N of Vernal at ~8,000 ft (aspen/pine forest, set back from Flaming Gorge Reservoir). ~35 sites, paved spurs, no hookups; water and RV dump available; mix of reservable and first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Beaver View Campground
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Evanston RD, Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (UT-150), ~34 mi S of Evanston at ~8,960 ft, alongside the Hayden Fork with beaver ponds nearby. 17 single sites (+1 group day-use), no hookups, no on-site water. Mix of reservable and first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Christmas Meadows Campground
note: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Evanston RD, ~36 mi from Evanston off UT-150 at ~8,800 ft, on a knoll above Stillwater Fork and Christmas Meadows. 10 sites, no hookups, drinking water, vault toilets; mix of reservable and first-come, first-served. Access road is unpaved/rocky but drivable in a normal vehicle. --Claude

name: Browne Lake Campground (Ashley NF)
note: USFS campground next to Browne Lake in a high mountain meadow (~8,200 ft), Flaming Gorge RD, Ashley NF, reached via well-maintained dirt road (FR-221 area). Single-family sites are first-come, first-served; four accessible group sites are separately reservable online. Picnic tables, campfire circles, vault toilets; no potable water. Fishing (rainbow/brook trout, kokanee) and non-motorized boating on Browne Lake. --Claude

name: Greendale Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: USFS Flaming Gorge NRA campground near the US-191/UT-44 junction, ~1 mi from Flaming Gorge Reservoir. 8 single sites (paved spurs, west of road) plus 2 group sites (dirt, up to 40 people, east of road); vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups. Single sites first-come, first-served; group sites reservable online. --Claude

name: Canyon Rim Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: USFS Flaming Gorge NRA campground in a grassy meadow ~7,400 ft above the reservoir on Red Canyon Rd (FR-095), near Greens Lake. ~17-18 sites (about 9 tent-only); family sites with picnic tables/fire rings, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; open ~mid-May to mid-Sep. Reservable online with some first-come, first-served sites. --Claude

name: Red Canyon Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: Small USFS Flaming Gorge campground (8 single gravel sites) in a meadow high on the Red Canyon rim above the reservoir, by the Red Canyon Visitor Center. Vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups; open ~mid-May to mid-Sep. Sites are small, un-level gravel spurs (best for rigs under ~26 ft; a 23-ft rig fits some). Mix of FCFS and reservable-online sites. --Claude

name: Indian Crossing Campground (Browns Park)
note: BLM campground in Browns Park along the Green River, adjacent to the historic John Jarvie Ranch day-use area. 20 individual sites + 1 group site, picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, no hookups. First-come, first-served — pay on-site (iron ranger, cash/check) or via the rec.gov Scan & Pay app. --Claude

name: Cedar Springs Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: USFS Flaming Gorge NRA campground on a pinyon/juniper hillside above the reservoir, <1 mi from Cedar Springs Marina. Single and double family sites, vault toilets, drinking water, dump station, fish-cleaning station (showers 0.5 mi at Deer Run); no hookups; many sites have reservoir views. Reservable online / some FCFS. --Claude

name: East Fork Bear River Campground (Uinta Mountains)
note: Small USFS campground on the Bear River off the Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (SR-150), ~8,300 ft in the Uintas near the Bear River Ranger Station. 7 single back-in sites (max vehicle length 25 ft), picnic tables/fire rings, vault toilet, hand-pump water, no hookups; concessionaire-operated, reservable online (season ~mid-June to early Sep) with day-of FCFS. --Claude

name: Dripping Springs Campground (Flaming Gorge)
note: USFS (Ashley NF, Flaming Gorge NRA) campground in high desert above the Green River near Little Hole, at the trailhead of the Little Hole NRT. 23 sites (some FCFS, most reservable), water spigots, vault toilets, no hookups, no dump station on site. Reservable online in season, FCFS off-season. --Claude

name: Carmel Campground (Flaming Gorge, Sheep Creek)
note: USFS (Ashley NF, Flaming Gorge NRA) campground along Sheep Creek on the Sheep Creek Geological Loop (FSR 218) off UT-44. 15 single-family sites for tents and smaller trailers/RVs; vault toilets, no drinking water, no hookups. First-come, first-served, open ~mid-May to mid-Sept. Bring water. --Claude

name: Marsh Lake (Uinta North Slope)
note: USFS campground on the north slope of the Uinta Mountains (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) beside Marsh Lake at ~9,400 ft; 44 sites in East (29) and West (15) loops plus 2 group sites, standard nonelectric (no hookups), drinking water and vault toilets, concessionaire-run. Mix of reservable and first-come, first-served sites; reservable online. Dump station ~1.5 mi away near Stateline. --Claude

name: Bridger Lake (Uinta North Slope)
note: USFS campground on the north slope of the Uinta Mountains (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) at Bridger Lake, ~9,400 ft; about 29 sites (single and double), standard/RV nonelectric (no hookups), two accessible sites with cement parking spurs, drinking water, vault toilets, camp host. Mix of reservable and first-come, first-served; reservable online. Dump station ~0.5 mi away. --Claude

name: Anderson Cove Campground (Pineview Reservoir)
note: USFS (Ogden RD, Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) high-standard campground on Pineview Reservoir, ~10 mi E of Ogden. 111 sites (58 single, 9 double, 9 yurts, 31 walk-to tent), nonelectric; vault toilets, drinking water, dump station, small general store, boat ramp and swim beach on site. Mostly reservable on recreation.gov with some FCFS. --Claude

name: Magpie Campground (South Fork Ogden)
note: Small USFS (Ogden RD, Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) campground on the South Fork Ogden River, ~5-7 mi E of Huntsville on Hwy 39. 10 sites (8 single, 2 double), standard nonelectric; picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets. Mix of reservable (recreation.gov) and FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Botts Campground (South Fork Ogden)
note: Small USFS (Ogden RD, Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) campground on the South Fork Ogden River, ~6 mi E of Huntsville on Hwy 39. 8 sites (7 single, 1 double), standard nonelectric; picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets. Mix of reservable (recreation.gov) and FCFS sites. --Claude

name: South Fork Campground (Ogden River)
note: USFS (Ogden RD, Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) campground on the banks of the South Fork Ogden River, ~7 mi E of Huntsville on Hwy 39. 44 single/double sites in two loops with cement pads, picnic tables, fire rings; vault toilets and drinking water. Loop A reservable on recreation.gov, other sites FCFS. Nonelectric. --Claude

name: Lower Meadows Campground (South Fork Ogden)
note: USFS (Ogden RD, Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) campground on the South Fork Ogden River, ~7 mi E of Huntsville on Hwy 39. 23 sites (17 single, 6 double), standard nonelectric; picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets. Mix of reservable (recreation.gov) and FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Upper Meadows Campground (South Fork Ogden)
note: Small USFS (Ogden RD, Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) campground on the South Fork Ogden River, ~7 mi E of Huntsville on Hwy 39, ~5,300 ft. 9 single sites, standard nonelectric; picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets. Reservable on recreation.gov with FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Willows Campground (South Fork Ogden)
note: USFS (Ogden RD, Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) campground on the South Fork Ogden River, easternmost of the South Fork loops, ~7 mi E of Huntsville on Hwy 39. 17 sites (14 single, 3 double), standard nonelectric; picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets. Mix of reservable (recreation.gov) and FCFS sites. --Claude

name: Box Elder Campground (Mantua)
note: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF) campground beside the town of Mantua ~5 mi from Brigham City; 29 single-family sites plus 4 group sites, gravel back-in pads for RVs to 40 ft, flush toilets, drinking water, no hookups; reservable on recreation.gov with some FCFS. Mantua Reservoir ~1 mi away. --Claude

name: Little Creek Campground
note: BLM (Salt Lake Field Office) campground 3 mi W of Randolph via Little Creek Rd (FS 058); 9 individual sites plus 1 group site, picnic tables, fire rings, parking areas, pit toilets, seasonal potable water, no hookups, no shade; sites 1-4 reservable on recreation.gov, 5-9 first-come, first-served. Little Creek Reservoir nearby. --Claude

name: Bridger Campground (Logan Canyon)
note: USFS (Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF, Logan RD) campground next to the Logan River ~6 mi E of Logan on US-89 (Logan Canyon Scenic Byway) at ~5,000 ft; 10 single sites, vault toilets, picnic tables and fire rings, no hookups; mix of reservable and first-come, first-served on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Sunrise Campground (Bear Lake)
note: USFS Uinta-Wasatch-Cache NF (Logan Ranger District), near Bear Lake Summit ~6 mi west of Garden City off US-89. 24 standard non-electric sites (2 yurts) in a wooded loop; paved roads and parking spurs, no hookups, drinking water and vault toilets. Mostly reservable online with some FCFS; roughly June-Oct. Limber Pine trailhead adjacent. First-come, first-served sites available. --Claude

name: Dead Horse Point State Park - Wingate Campground
note: Newer of Dead Horse Point SP's two campgrounds (Kayenta already listed, id 281), atop the mesa by the visitor center. 20 electric RV/tent sites (plus 11 hike-in tent sites and 4 yurts, not counted); RVs to 56 ft; shade shelters, flush restrooms, dump station at entrance. No potable water for RV fill anywhere in the park. Reservable via ReserveAmerica, FCFS if unbooked. --Claude

name: Green River State Park
note: Utah State Park on the Green River in the town of Green River, beside a 9-hole golf course. 38 RV sites (34 full-hookup, 4 electric/water) shaded by mature cottonwoods; dump station at the boat ramp; spacious sites fit large rigs. Some FCFS, some reservable via ReserveAmerica. Open year-round. --Claude

name: East Canyon State Park
note: Utah State Park on East Canyon Reservoir near Morgan. North-side Dixie Campground has 32 sites with full and partial RV hookups (fire rings, picnic tables), open year-round with limited winter services; south side has the primitive Big Rock area (21 sites) plus group sites. Reservable via ReserveAmerica (roughly May-Sep), FCFS off-season. Pinned to the Dixie loop on the NE shore. --Claude

name: Echo State Park - Dry Hollow Campground
note: Dry Hollow Campground at Echo State Park (Echo Reservoir), Coalville. 18 standard sites with water and 20/30/50-amp electric (no sewer), plus restroom/shower building and a group area with 5 partial-hookup spots; each site has picnic table, fire ring and shelter. Reservable via ReserveAmerica May 1-Sep 30; FCFS Oct-Apr with water/restrooms shut down. Pinned to the loop on the reservoir's E shore. --Claude

name: Hyrum State Park
note: Hyrum State Park on Hyrum Reservoir, ~8 mi SW of Logan. 32-site campground on the reservoir's N shore with 2 water+electric sites and 10 electric sites; most sites accommodate larger RVs. Reservable via ReserveAmerica (2+ days ahead) or FCFS via self-pay envelope off-peak. Pinned to the shoreline camp loop above the beach. --Claude

name: Bear Lake State Park - Cisco Beach Campground
note: Utah State Parks, Bear Lake Eastside. Cisco Beach is a primitive beachfront campground of ~59 individual sites strung along the shore; vault toilets, no hookups, low-water boat launch on the south end. First-come, first-served (the park's only FCFS campground), open year-round. --Claude

name: Lincoln Beach Campground
note: Utah County park on the south shore of Utah Lake near Lincoln Point, at the Lincoln Beach boat harbor/ramp. 8 primitive no-hookup back-in tent/RV sites (most ~40 ft), picnic tables, fire pits, restrooms, water spigots; boat ramp on site. Largely first-come, first-served (limited online booking, 3-day max). --Claude

name: Nunn's Park
note: Utah County park in lower Provo Canyon along US-189, on the Provo River near Bridal Veil Falls and the Provo River Parkway trail. Primitive tent/RV sites with parking spurs, coal grills, fire pits, vault toilets (no showers); most sites ~$20 ($30 by the playground). Best suited to smaller RVs and tents; mostly first-come, first-served. RV Life unrated (0)/$ (auto 7/2026). --Claude

name: Weber Memorial Park
note: Weber County park in the South Fork Ogden River bottom below Causey Reservoir, east of Huntsville. 58 individual sites (first-come, first-served, fee paid on-site to the camp host) plus 5 group areas (A, B North, B South, C, Lodge -- reservable via Sportsites); an individual site takes one trailer + one tent; limited electricity in Areas B and C, otherwise dry camping; fire pits and picnic tables. Open first weekend of May to early October, weather permitting. First-come, first-served for individual sites. --Claude

name: North Fork Park
note: Weber County park on the east side of the Wasatch above Liberty/Eden, 2,600 acres. ~132 individual dry-camping sites across five areas (Cold Water, Cutler Flats, Loop A/B/Corrals, Middle Gate, Mustang Flats); no electric/water hookups, running water and flush toilets, fire pits, picnic tables, horse corrals. Travel trailers and pull-through sites are accommodated but the loop roads are narrow dirt, so it's best for smaller rigs; a 23-ft rig fits the drive-in sites. Group sites reservable; individual sites first-come, first-served (no reservations). Open first weekend of May to mid-October, weather permitting. --Claude

name: Sleeping Bear Campground
note: Navajo family-owned primitive drive-in campground off Douglas Mesa Rd (Hwy 163) in Monument Valley; spacious sites with picnic tables and fire rings, no hookups, no water/showers, outhouse only. Decent dirt access road; firsthand reviews report 8 m and 32-ft Class A RVs parked with no issue. First-come, first-served, ~$25/night. --Claude
